title: Intensive versus standard blood-pressure control in adults at increased cardiovascular risk: evidence report

subject.display: PICO: Intensive versus standard blood-pressure control for major adverse cardiovascular events in adults at increased cardiovascular risk

extension.valueMarkdown: An evidence report summarising the effect of intensive versus standard blood-pressure control on major adverse cardiovascular events in adults aged 50 years or older with hypertension and increased cardiovascular risk, excluding adults with diabetes mellitus.
Provides the evidence base for a guideline recommendation on systolic blood-pressure targets in primary and secondary cardiovascular prevention.

valueCodeableConcept.text: Adults aged 50 years or older with hypertension and increased cardiovascular risk, excluding adults with diabetes mellitus
Intensive blood-pressure control: antihypertensive therapy titrated to a systolic target below 120 mmHg
Standard blood-pressure control: antihypertensive therapy titrated to a systolic target below 140 mmHg
Major adverse cardiovascular events: composite of myocardial infarction, other acute coronary syndrome, stroke, acute decompensated heart failure, or death from cardiovascular causes
